propositions: scc_loc.analyze() invokes scc via subprocess.run with --format json, parses the two-level JSON structure (language groups containing per-file entries), and returns AnalyzerResult with loc={"files": {relpath: loc_int}, "max_loc": max_int}
When scc is unavailable (binary missing, non-zero exit, empty/unparseable stdout), analyze() returns Unavailable(reason, _ACCRUING_SINCE) with a logged warning, never returning zeros or crashing
Successful output with zero files yields AnalyzerResult(loc={"files": {}, "max_loc": 0}), not Unavailable
Location paths from scc JSON are converted to repo-relative POSIX-normalized keys using os.path.relpath() and PurePath.as_posix()
The run parameter is injectable for testing, allowing tests to provide canned scc JSON without requiring live scc binary
scc_loc.py remains self-contained in analyzers/ package without importing from rebar.grounding, preserving clean layering and avoiding metrics<->grounding coupling
